game.name: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth
game.short_description: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth is a randomly generated action RPG shooter with heavy Rogue-like elements. Following Isaac on his journey players will find bizarre treasures that change Isaac’s form giving him super human abilities and enabling him to fight off droves of mysterious creatures, discover secrets and fight his way to safety.

placements.verbal_evidence: of course this this is an easy s tier there's no doubt about that

commentary.label: Tier list Part 1 (2023)
commentary.summary: The Binding of Isaac is the top-down roguelite that helped bring the genre back to modern gaming, and he calls it probably the most packed roguelite around. He says it is the one game he could play forever because it never gets old. He has over 300 hours in it and notes it keeps receiving new content. He places it in S tier without hesitation and tells viewers who haven't played it to go play it.
praise: Enormous amount of content: many characters, items and things to do
Characters play very differently from one another
Huge item pool that still feels balanced despite the power-fantasy moments
Plenty of depth to master and endless replayability
Still being updated with new content after all these years
criticism: No real criticisms; he says there is nothing left to say that has not already been said
Admits he has not played much of the newest content
unique_points: Helped revive roguelikes and roguelites in the modern era
Makes the player feel overpowered at times yet retains mastery depth
Sheer density of content makes it feel like the most packed roguelite available
commentary.quote: it never gets old you can always come back to it
design_criteria: Content volume: characters, items and secrets in huge quantity
Character diversity: each character plays distinctly
Balance and power fantasy: feels overpowered sometimes but still balanced
Replayability: never gets old, long-term play

community.one_liner: A twin-stick, room-by-room dungeon crawler by Edmund McMillen where Isaac descends through randomly generated floors collecting hundreds of synergistic items, wrapped in grotesque religious-horror imagery.
community.consensus_summary: Regarded as one of the defining roguelikes: Steam shows 96.8% positive across about 459k reviews (Overwhelmingly Positive) and critics landed in the high 80s for Rebirth (Metacritic 88 on 15 reviews, OpenCritic 87 with 92% recommending). Players praise near-endless replayability from 700+ items and 34 characters, tight shooting, and the bleak-funny identity. The recurring complaints are RNG swings, opaque item text, a long unlock and completion grind, and steep difficulty for newcomers. The game is fully released and very much alive: Repentance is the final expansion and the community keeps it going with mods and Workshop content, and a 2026 patch triggered some DLC-loading complaints on Steam.
best_things: Huge replayability: 700+ items, 188 trinkets, 34 characters (with Tainted versions) and thousands of hours are cited by long-time players
Item synergies produce wildly different builds each run (Brimstone, Tech X and similar combos are commonly named as highlights)
Tight, responsive twin-stick combat with a fast, addictive 'one more run' loop
Strong, committed dark and gross aesthetic with a memorable soundtrack and a story told through endings and secrets
Repentance rebalanced overpowered and weak items, added new routes, bosses and thousands of rooms; one review gave the DLC 9.5/10
Very good value, especially on sale, given the content volume; Steam Workshop mods extend it further
Hidden secrets and discoverable mechanics reward curiosity and community knowledge-sharing
worst_things: Item effects are poorly explained in-game, so many players rely on mods or the wiki to know what pickups do
Heavy RNG: item pools are bloated, so bad rolls and unwinnable seeds are common, and top players restart early floors until they find a strong first item
Hostile onboarding: new players report difficulty even learning controls and the game's systems, with little guidance
Some content gates are harsh: powerful items like Godhead and Death Certificate require beating hard late bosses, sometimes with one-hit characters like The Lost
Repentance-era balance: trap rooms and sudden damage can ruin runs regardless of knowledge; Delirium is described as broken by teleporting onto the player
Multiplayer/co-op reportedly desyncs, and you cannot rejoin mid-floor
Darker themes (child abuse, religious extremism) and crude humor put some players off; content is not for younger players
Recent patches reportedly broke DLC loading or launch (Afterbirth+/Repentance), with some players rolling back to older versions and unable to refund
improvements: Better in-game item descriptions or an optional info display (the most popular mod simply tells you what items do)
A gentler tutorial/onboarding so new players learn controls and core systems
Less RNG dependence and tighter item pool curation so runs feel less dependent on early luck
Fewer time-gated and grindy completion requirements (daily challenges, repeated hard-mode clears)
More reliable online co-op and better patch QA so DLC does not break after updates
unique_things: Extremely dense item-interaction system with 700+ items, giving emergent builds no other roguelike matches in raw variety
Shoot-in-four-directions dungeon crawl structure with Zelda-style rooms instead of continuous levels
Uncompromising religious-horror and body-horror theme paired with cartoon visuals and dark comedy
Completion meta with 34 characters, dozens of endings and a 'Dead God' 100% achievement that can take 500+ hours
Shaped the modern roguelite genre; the series originated from a Flash game in 2011 and was remade in Rebirth in 2014
tedious_or_disliked: 100% completion and unlocks are a long grind, cited as 500+ hours, including killing final bosses repeatedly across many characters
Daily challenges act as real-calendar time gates for certain unlocks, which players compare to mobile-game design
Restarting early floors or rerolling until the item pool looks promising, and slower clears when pools are diluted (a reported habit, not a top review theme)
Hard-mode requirements for best unlocks feel punishing for casual players
Some players dislike specific characters or modes (Jacob and Esau, Curse of the Blind, Lazarus, Tainted Lost are named in reviews)
Four-way shooting and enemy design feel restrictive or boring to a minority, with hitbox or movement complaints in a few reviews
Forced modes for unlocks, e.g. Greed Mode, are said to stall enjoyment of the core game
divisive_points: RNG versus skill: critics call it luck-driven, while defenders point to long win streaks by top players as proof skill dominates
Repentance: many see a masterpiece of content and balance, others feel it added chores and pushed difficulty toward hardcore players
Low-information design: some love discovering item effects by experiment, others find it poor design
Art style and tone: praised as distinctive and funny by fans, dismissed as teenage-edgy or off-putting by others
community.reception_notes: The 2011 Flash original sold about 700k copies in under a year and passed 2 million by late 2012 (per news reports), which funded the Rebirth remake by McMillen and Nicalis (Nov 2014, new engine, co-op, hundreds of new items). Afterbirth, Afterbirth+ and the 2021 Repentance expansion followed (OpenCritic 88, 82 and 83 per search results). Steam-revenue-calculator estimates for Rebirth are about $225M gross and about $66M net (Boxleiter-style, order-of-magnitude only); SteamSpy lists 5 to 10 million owners. Metacritic page re-fetched: Metascore 88 on 15 reviews, user 8.2 on 1,154 ratings. Current Steam reviews (2026) are still overwhelmingly positive, with many ironic 'I hate this game' recommendations from 1000+ hour players, a few complaints about a recent patch breaking DLC loading, and multiplayer desync complaints.
